question.text: Find the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(-w,7z)$ and $(5w,-3z).$
question.explanation:
Let $(x_m,y_m)$ be the midpoint between $\underbrace{(-w,7z)}_{\text{($x_1$,$\;y_1)$}}$ and $\underbrace{(5w,-3z)}_{\text{($x_2$,$\;y_2)$}}.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

\[ \eqalign{ (x_m,y_m) &= \left(\dfrac{x_1 +x_2}2,\dfrac{y_1+y_2}2\right) \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{-w+5w}2,\dfrac{7z+(-3z)}2\right)\\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{-w+5w}2,\dfrac{7z-3z}2\right) \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{4w}2,\dfrac{4z}2\right) \\[5pt] &= (2w, 2z). } \]

question.text: Find the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(8p,-q)$ and $(-2p,-9q).$
question.explanation:
Let $(x_m,y_m)$ be the midpoint between $\underbrace{(8p,-q)}_{\text{($x_1$,$\;y_1)$}}$ and $\underbrace{(-2p,-9q)}_{\text{($x_2$,$\;y_2)$}}.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

\[ \eqalign{ (x_m,y_m) &= \left(\dfrac{x_1 +x_2}2,\dfrac{y_1+y_2}2\right) \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{8p+(-2p)}2,\dfrac{-q+(-9q)}2\right)\\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{8p-2p}2,\dfrac{-q-9q}2\right) \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{6p}2,\dfrac{-10q}2\right) \\[5pt] &= (3p, -5q). } \]

example.title: Finding the Midpoint of a Segment With Variable Coordinates

question.text: Given that $(1,1)$ is the midpoint of the line segment $\overline{PQ}$ above, find the values of $a$ and $b.$
question.explanation:
The given points are $\underbrace{(a,b)}_{\text{($x_1,\,y_1)$}}$, $\underbrace{(-2,0)}_{\text{($x_2,\,y_2)$}}$ and $\underbrace{(1,1)}_{\text{($x_m,\,y_m)$}}.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows: \begin{align} (x_m,y_m) & = \left(\dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right) \\[5pt] (1,1) & = \left(\dfrac{a - 2}{2}, \dfrac{b + 0}{2}\right) \end{align}

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us \begin{align*} \begin{cases} 1 = \dfrac{a - 2}{2} \\[5pt] 1 = \dfrac{b}{2} \end{cases} \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} a = 4 \\[3pt] b = 2. \end{cases} \end{align*}

Thus, $a=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}$ and $b=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}.$
